# Project plan

## Start-up phase
<!--
Covering the planning phase, this section should provide a relatively
detailed plan of how work will start on the project. This section is
important because projects need to get up and running quickly.


 - [ ] Setting up collaboration platform inc. code for contributors etc.
 - [ ] License decisions
 - [ ] Reporting framework
-->

The start-up phase will consist of the basic steps to set up the project:

- a public GitHub repository under the MIT licence, with issues used to track all work
- a name for the tool, checked against CRAN, crates.io and GitHub
- an announcement post on the R Consortium blog

## Technical delivery
<!--
Covering the actual delivery of the project this section should
provide at least a high-level description of the implementation.

Including target dates is really important as you need to be committed
and the ISC need to have a means of tracking delivery
-->

A proof-of-concept already exists at [doclint-prototype](https://github.com/thisisnic/doclint-prototype), which confirms that air's parser can be used from a standalone Rust project and that roxygen comments can be extracted with correct line numbers.

Although the prototype contains a reasonably advanced initial implementation, it was developed almost entirely with AI-generated code and little human oversight. 
The parser implementation during the project itself will involve a more thorough examination of library design, based on project goals and best practices, with a focus on ensuring the resulting code is well understood by the package author and suitable for a collaborative open source project.

### Milestone 1 - 31st January 2027: design document, maintainer conversations, working parser and first rule

The initial phase covers in-depth project design, which will be completed ahead of full technical implementation.
This will include a deep dive on the different options, examining design decisions made in related projects like air, jarl, and Vale and properly break down the project into key requirements.

The design document will covers the text segment model, the rule interface, whether rules are defined as code or as data, the configuration format, and how lints are mapped back to source lines.

Alongside this, requirements around specific rules will be generated by consultation with prominent package maintainers, and a review of the documentation feedback given in public software review threads, such as rOpenSci's, to determine what subset of rules will be most useful for an initial default ruleset implementation.

The code delivered from this stage is the parser layer, the text layer, an initial subset of rules, and a command-line interface, with snapshot tests, updated from the prototype.

### Milestone 2 - 28th February 2027: core rules, Markdown sources, config, JSON output and developer preview.

Core rules will be full specified here, with examples of passes and failures, and explained in the project documentation.

The code delivered is the remaining core rules, vignette and README support via a Markdown parser, the configuration file, and JSON output.
The milestone ends with a developer preview on GitHub Releases, announced publicly with an issue template for reporting rules that misfire, so that feedback arrives while there is still time to act on it.
Complete when the core rules exist, including reference pages and snapshot tests, and the public preview is published.

### Milestone 3 - 31st March 2027 - validation report, external code review, release and GitHub Action.

Feedback from the preview and a run over the 100 most downloaded CRAN packages together drive tuning of the rules and defaults, and a report is published showing hits per rule and what changed as a result.

The code delivered is binaries for Linux, macOS and Windows on GitHub Releases, and a GitHub Action so that linting can automatically be run on CI jobs as part of the package development process.

Complete when the release is tagged, the report is published and the review findings are closed.

### Milestone 4 - 30th April 2027 - error message linting, pre-commit hook, AGENTS.md command, R wrapper and contributor guide

The final phase completes all remaining key requirements and features initially identified. This includes error message linting, a pre-commit hook, a command that writes the active rules into a project's AGENTS.md file, and a thin R package that installs and runs the binary.

It will also include a contributor guide explaining how to add a rule.

Complete when each is shipped and documented, and a closing post on the R Consortium blog reports what changed across the project as a result of feedback.

## Other aspects

<!--
How will you ensure that your work is available to the widest number
of people? Please specify the open-source or creative commons license(s)
you will use, how you will host your code so that others can contribute,
and how you will publicize your work. We encourage you to plan content
to be shared quarterly on the R Consortium blog.

 - [ ] Announcement post
 - [ ] Delivery blog post
 - [ ] Social media
 - [ ] UseR!
 - [ ] ISC meetings
-->

All code is released under the MIT licence and developed in the open on GitHub, with issues used for tracking so that progress is visible throughout.
Binaries will be published on GitHub Releases, and the R wrapper package will be submitted to CRAN.

The work will be publicised with an announcement post and a closing post on the R Consortium blog, posts on LinkedIn, Mastodon and Bluesky at each milestone, submission to R Weekly, and a talk submitted to an R conference in 2027.

## Budget & funding plan

<!--
Note that the maximum grant is $10k USD. The proposal should be in USD.

Outline the milestones for development and how much funding will be

We expect that most of the budget will be allocated

The budget is labour only, at USD 65 per hour, covering 100 hours of part-time work over four months.
External reviews are unpaid.
There are no other costs, as the project uses GitHub for hosting, CI and releases.

| Milestone | Target | Hours | USD |
|-----------|--------|------:|----:|
| 1: Design document, maintainer conversations, working parser, first rules and developer preview | 31 Jan 2027 | 40 | 2,600 |
| 2: Core rules, Markdown sources, config, JSON output and public preview | 28 Feb 2027 | 20 | 1,300 |
| 3: Validation report, release and GitHub Action | 31 Mar 2027 | 15 | 975 |
| 4: Error message linting, pre-commit hook, AGENTS.md command, R wrapper and contributor guide | 30 Apr 2027 | 25 | 1,625 |
| **Total** | | **100** | **6,500** |
